_note: Sources for the staged library (library.json), same shape as sources.json. Keys used in library.json resolve here or in sources.json. Pages were read on 2026-10-01 (PDB-101 Molecule of the Month, OpenStax, PubChem PUG View record descriptions, Europe PMC abstracts). RCSB entry and CCD facts (title, chains, ligands, organism, method, resolution, formula) were read from the downloaded mmCIF file itself with tools/library_facts.py.

motm-1.cite: PDB-101 Molecule of the Month: Myoglobin (January 2000).
motm-1.checked: 2026-10-01: small, bright red protein, common in muscle cells, gives meat much of its red colour; stores oxygen for when muscles work hard; John Kendrew and coworkers determined its structure; first protein to have its atomic structure determined.

motm-6.cite: PDB-101 Molecule of the Month: HIV-1 Protease (June 2000).
motm-6.checked: 2026-10-01: cuts the long polyprotein into protein-sized pieces; two identical chains of 99 amino acids; a tunnel covered by two flexible flaps; drugs mimic a protein chain but cannot be cleaved; ritonavir shown with entry 1hxw.

motm-7.cite: PDB-101 Molecule of the Month: Nucleosome (July 2000).
motm-7.checked: 2026-10-01: eight histone proteins bundled together, encircled by two loops of DNA; nucleosomes protect DNA strands from physical damage; intact nucleosome in entry 1aoi.

motm-11.cite: PDB-101 Molecule of the Month: Rubisco (November 2000).
motm-11.checked: 2026-10-01: attaches carbon dioxide to ribulose bisphosphate, a five-carbon sugar; most plentiful single enzyme on Earth; fixes only about three carbon dioxide molecules per second; plant form has eight large and eight small chains; 8ruc named.

motm-12.cite: PDB-101 Molecule of the Month: Pepsin (December 2000).
motm-12.checked: 2026-10-01: digests proteins in strong stomach acid; protein chains bind in its deep active-site groove and are broken into smaller pieces; works best in strong hydrochloric acid; made with an extra 44 amino acids that block the groove and are clipped off in the stomach.

motm-21.cite: PDB-101 Molecule of the Month: Antibodies (September 2001).
motm-21.checked: 2026-10-01: circulate in the blood scrutinizing every object they touch; four chains, two long heavy and two shorter light; binding site at the tips of the two arms between light and heavy chain; antibody from entry 1igt shown.

motm-22.cite: PDB-101 Molecule of the Month: Photosystem I (October 2001).
motm-22.checked: 2026-10-01: chlorophyll absorbs blue and red light, leaving greens for us to see; chlorophyll contains magnesium; when chlorophylls capture light an electron is excited into a higher energy state.

motm-38.cite: PDB-101 Molecule of the Month: Potassium Channels (February 2003).
motm-38.checked: 2026-10-01: allow potassium to flow across the membrane while blocking other ions; one sodium ion passes for every ten thousand potassium ions; four identical proteins forming a pore down the centre; nerve cells concentrate potassium inside and pump sodium out before a signal; bacterial channel from entry 1bl8.

motm-54.cite: PDB-101 Molecule of the Month: Acetylcholinesterase (June 2004).
motm-54.checked: 2026-10-01: breaks acetylcholine into acetic acid and choline, stopping the signal; each in about 80 microseconds; active site in a deep pocket; partial blocking drugs raise neurotransmitter levels (Alzheimer's); first studied in electric fish such as the torpedo ray; 1acj shown.

motm-62.cite: PDB-101 Molecule of the Month: Major Histocompatibility Complex (February 2005).
motm-62.checked: 2026-10-01: class I MHC on the surface of most cells protects from viral infection; cells display pieces of old proteins on their surfaces; each person has their own MHC types and grafts with different types trigger the immune system; human MHC called HLA; 1hsa named.

motm-64.cite: PDB-101 Molecule of the Month: Kinesin (April 2005).
motm-64.checked: 2026-10-01: carries cargo along microtubules, crawling hand over hand; cells built three types of ATP-powered motors; kinesin in entry 3kin is two chains with two motor domains holding ADP.

motm-66.cite: PDB-101 Molecule of the Month: Carotenoid Oxygenase (June 2005).
motm-66.checked: 2026-10-01: the colour of carrots and many orange and yellow vegetables comes from carotenoids such as beta-carotene; long thin molecules with a string of carbon-carbon double bonds that absorb light; our cells break beta-carotene in half to form two molecules of retinal.

motm-71.cite: PDB-101 Molecule of the Month: Acetylcholine Receptor (November 2005).
motm-71.checked: 2026-10-01: receptors on muscle cells at the nerve-muscle synapse; acetylcholine binding changes the receptor shape and opens the channel; acetylcholinesterase breaks the neurotransmitter down.

motm-100.cite: PDB-101 Molecule of the Month: Adrenergic Receptors (April 2008).
motm-100.checked: 2026-10-01: adrenaline (epinephrine) tells cells to ready themselves in danger, the flight or fight response; released into the blood from the adrenal glands on top of the kidneys; raises heart rate and blood sugar; digestion temporarily halted.

motm-147.cite: PDB-101 Molecule of the Month: Rhodopsin (March 2012).
motm-147.checked: 2026-10-01: the molecule that senses light; retinal absorbs a photon and one bond flips from bent (cis) to extended (trans); rod cells can be triggered by a single photon; launches a G-protein signal leading to a nerve signal to the brain; 1f88 shown.

motm-164.cite: PDB-101 Molecule of the Month: Serotonin Receptor (August 2013).
motm-164.checked: 2026-10-01: serotonin is made from the amino acid tryptophan; controls happiness, hunger and more, emotions and moods; most of the body's serotonin is in the digestive system controlling the motions of digestion; fluoxetine (Prozac) blocks reuptake.

motm-171.cite: PDB-101 Molecule of the Month: Neurotransmitter Transporters (March 2014).
motm-171.checked: 2026-10-01: transporters clear neurotransmitters out of the synaptic cleft, powered by sodium and chloride; antidepressants and cocaine block dopamine transporters.

motm-250.cite: PDB-101 Molecule of the Month: Capsaicin Receptor TRPV1 (October 2020).
motm-250.checked: 2026-10-01: capsaicin in chili peppers protects the plant; TRPV1 is an ion channel opened by capsaicin and also when the temperature gets very hot; it lets us sense both heat and spicy food with similar sensations.

motm-288.cite: PDB-101 Molecule of the Month: Vitamins (December 2023).
motm-288.checked: 2026-10-01: vitamin C (ascorbic acid) is a powerful antioxidant that restores the iron atoms of collagen prolyl 4-hydroxylase; sailors got scurvy, a disease of being unable to build collagen, from lack of vitamin C; our cells cannot make vitamins so we get them from food.

os-3-2-sucrose.checked: 2026-10-01: sucrose, or table sugar, is glucose and fructose monomers joined in a dehydration reaction by a glycosidic bond.

os-3-4-roles.checked: 2026-10-01: protein-types table lists keratin as a structural protein, pepsin as a digestive enzyme, immunoglobulins as defence proteins that protect the body from foreign pathogens.

os-21-1.cite: OpenStax Biology 2e, section 21.1 Viral Evolution, Morphology, and Classification.
os-21-1.checked: 2026-10-01: all virions have a nucleic acid genome covered by a protective capsid; capsid proteins are encoded in the viral genome (capsomeres); icosahedral viruses are roughly spherical; viruses are noncellular and complete replication inside a host cell.

os-35-2.cite: OpenStax Biology 2e, section 35.2 How Neurons Communicate.
os-35-2.checked: 2026-10-01: acetylcholine released at the neuromuscular junction opens sodium channels; some drugs for Alzheimer's patients inhibit acetylcholinesterase, the enzyme that degrades acetylcholine; dopamine and serotonin listed as biogenic amine neurotransmitters.

os-37-5.checked: 2026-10-01: oxytocin is produced by neurons in the hypothalamus and transported along their axons to the posterior pituitary; the pituitary secretes peptide or protein hormones; oxytocin stimulates uterine contractions during childbirth and milk ejection.

pubchem-187.checked: 2026-10-01 (PUG View Record Description): ester of acetic acid and choline acting as a neurotransmitter (ChEBI); the major transmitter at neuromuscular junctions in vertebrates (DrugBank).

pubchem-681.checked: 2026-10-01 (PUG View Record Description): one of the catecholamine neurotransmitters in the brain; derived from tyrosine and the precursor to norepinephrine and epinephrine; important in regulating movement (DrugBank).

pubchem-1548943.checked: 2026-10-01 (PUG View Record Description): primary pungent principle in Capsicum fruits (T3DB); TRPV1 agonist (PubChem summary); used as a topical analgesic in creams, liquids and patches (DrugBank).

pubchem-2519.checked: 2026-10-01 (PUG View Record Description): trimethylxanthine (ChEBI); major component of coffee, tea and chocolate, acts as a central nervous system stimulant (LiverTox); structurally related to adenosine, acts primarily as an adenosine receptor antagonist (NCI Thesaurus).

pubchem-5202.checked: 2026-10-01 (PUG View Record Description): monoamine messenger (ChEBI); synthesized from L-tryptophan, found mainly in the central nervous system, gastrointestinal tract and blood platelets (MeSH).

pubchem-5816.checked: 2026-10-01 (PUG View Record Description): also known as adrenaline, a hormone and neurotransmitter produced by the adrenal glands (DrugBank); increases the force and rate of heart contraction (NCI Thesaurus); used for anaphylactic reactions (DrugBank).

pubchem-5988.checked: 2026-10-01 (PUG View Record Description): nonreducing disaccharide of glucose and fructose; obtained commercially from sugarcane, sugar beet and other plants; used extensively as a food and a sweetener (DrugBank).

osc-2-6.cite: OpenStax Chemistry 2e, section 2.6 Ionic and Molecular Compounds.
osc-2-6.checked: 2026-10-01: compounds are ionic or molecular; a sodium cation has lost an electron; each sodium atom gives up one electron and each chlorine atom accepts one, so NaCl has one Na+ for each Cl-; ionic bonds are electrostatic attractions between ions of opposite charge; an ionic compound is not made of discrete molecules; sodium chloride melts at 801 C while water melts at 0 C; H2O2, the bleach and disinfectant, is molecular (Example 2.12).

osc-11-5.checked: 2026-10-01: salts of fatty acids are called soaps; sodium stearate, C17H35CO2Na, has an uncharged nonpolar hydrocarbon chain and an ionic carboxylate group; the hydrocarbon end dissolves in or is attracted to oil, grease or dirt; the ionic end is attracted by water; soap acts as a bridge between nonpolar and polar matter and emulsifies oil drops in water.
